study.title: A Convolutional-Transformer Model for FFR and iFR Assessment From Coronary Angiography

imaging.modality_detail: X-ray catheter coronary angiography videos; native 512x512 to 1024x1024 at 15-60 fps, resized to 256x256 and resampled to 15 fps
imaging.territory_detail: Coronary arteries, intermediate single coronary stenoses (CCS and ACS patients)
imaging.frames_per_sequence: 60 frames (4 central seconds at 15 fps; padded by frame replication if shorter)

annotation.annotator_expertise: Expert cardiologists (per hospital); labels derived from invasive FFR/iFR measurements thresholded at 0.80/0.89

task.task_description: Single-view angiography video classification of hemodynamically significant coronary stenosis (FFR<0.80 / iFR<0.89) with direct FFR and iFR regression via multi-branch heads, without key frame selection
task.clinical_application: Non-invasive angiography-based functional assessment of intermediate coronary stenosis to support revascularization decisions

temporal_evidence.quote: attention is computed between concatenated frame-level feature vectors

method.class_imbalance_handling: Random oversampling of positive class; balanced binary cross-entropy

G2.quote: we plan to carry out a more extensive assessment including more data from different geographical areas to enhance the applicability of the proposed approach

G3.quote: our method learns blood flow dynamics throughout the entire cycle

G4.quote: it is not able to reconstruct the geometry of arterial structures, for which FFR-CT procedure is required

G7.quote: To further enhance trust in our model, we also evaluate interpretability maps

G8.quote: We thus aim also to extend our approach with CT data to complement our findings

G9.quote: to deal with the overrepresentation of negative cases, we employed random oversampling

G10.quote: to share data in a privacy-preserving way

other_limitations: Validated only on single coronary lesions, not diffuse disease
Lower sensitivity attributed to hard clinical cut-off
FFR vs iFR ablation on small 81-case subset
future_work: More data from different geographical areas
Synthetic data generation for augmentation and privacy-preserving data sharing
